model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^4. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3, though the axis extends visually beyond 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and spans from 40% to 65%, with tick marks every 5 percentage points. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 38% accuracy and increases slightly to around 43% as co-occurrence number grows. The FT method (blue line with triangular markers) begins at about 40% and rises to approximately 47%. The IKE method (red line with triangular markers) starts at roughly 43% and reaches about 49%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at approximately 44% and increases to about 56%. The MEMIT method (purple line with diamond markers) starts at around 44% and rises to about 54%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) exhibits the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and increasing to about 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All lines show a general upward trend, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the entire range.
